issues.legal_issue: A transfer of non-agricultural land by an under-tenant can activate the immediate landlord’s right to seek transfer of the land.
material_facts: The transferors held the disputed land as under-tenants under a permanent lease.
The claimant was the immediate landlord in relation to the disputed land, although its interest in that land was limited to receiving rent.
The under-tenants transferred their rights in the land to a third party, and the immediate landlord applied for the land to be transferred to it.
issues.conclusion: The statutory right applied to the transfer by the under-tenants, and the immediate landlord was entitled to apply for the land to be transferred to it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(3), 3 and 24 of the West Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, the Act recognizes tenants and under-tenants as classes of non-agricultural tenant; an under-tenant is a tenant for the purposes of the Act. Section 23 requires notice of a transfer, and section 24 permits the immediate landlord to apply following the transfer. The landlord’s limited interest in receiving rent did not alter its status as immediate landlord.

rule.if: landlord_transfer_claim and non_agricultural_land_transferred and transferor_is_under_tenant and claimant_is_immediate_landlord

predicates.landlord_transfer_claim: An immediate landlord applied to have transferred land that its tenant had transferred to another person.
predicates.non_agricultural_land_transferred: The land transferred was held as non-agricultural land.
predicates.transferor_is_under_tenant: The person who transferred the land held it as an under-tenant.
predicates.claimant_is_immediate_landlord: The applicant was the person immediately above the transferring holder in the landlord-tenant relationship.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks transfer of non-agricultural land transferred by its under-tenant, and the applicant is the immediate landlord, the under-tenant’s status does not prevent the landlord’s transfer right from being triggered.

issues.legal_issue: An immediate landlord satisfies the statutory conditions for seeking transfer when the transferred land is contiguous to land in its actual possession and is bona fide required for a permitted use.
material_facts: The disputed land was contiguous to land in the immediate landlord’s actual possession.
The immediate landlord bona fide required the land to expand its educational institution.
The court found that the intended use fell within the permitted purposes for which non-agricultural land could be held.
issues.conclusion: The statutory conditions were satisfied because the land was contiguous to land in the landlord’s actual possession and was bona fide required for a permitted purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 24 of the West Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act requires the transferred land to be contiguous to land in the immediate landlord’s actual possession and requires the court to be satisfied that the land is needed for a purpose specified in section 4. The court treated expansion of the educational institution as falling within the permitted business or other purposes.

rule.if: landlord_transfer_claim and non_agricultural_land_transferred and land_contiguous_to_landlord_possession and landlord_bona_fide_requires_land and intended_use_is_permitted

predicates.landlord_transfer_claim: An immediate landlord applied to have transferred land that its tenant had transferred to another person.
predicates.non_agricultural_land_transferred: The land transferred was held as non-agricultural land.
predicates.land_contiguous_to_landlord_possession: The transferred land adjoined land actually possessed by the immediate landlord.
predicates.landlord_bona_fide_requires_land: The immediate landlord genuinely required the transferred land for its own use.
predicates.intended_use_is_permitted: The landlord’s intended use of the transferred land was among the purposes permitted for non-agricultural land.

issues.definition: An immediate landlord meets the transfer eligibility conditions when it seeks transferred non-agricultural land that adjoins land it actually possesses and genuinely needs for a permitted use.

issues.legal_issue: A non-agricultural tenant is excluded from the category of intermediary for the purpose of determining whether its interests vested in the State.
material_facts: The claimant held the larger plot, including the disputed land, as a non-agricultural tenant.
The claimant was the immediate landlord of the under-tenants and was entitled to receive rent from them.
The dispute concerned whether the claimant’s interest vested in the State under the estates acquisition legislation.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not an intermediary within the statutory definition, so its interest did not vest in the State on that basis and it could apply for transfer of the land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(i) of the West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act defines an intermediary by reference to specified interests above a raiyat or non-agricultural tenant. A person that is itself a non-agricultural tenant is excluded from that definition.

predicates.estate_vesting_status_dispute: A dispute arose over whether a landholder’s interest vested in the State as an intermediary.
predicates.claimant_is_non_agricultural_tenant: The landholder whose status was disputed held the land as a non-agricultural tenant.

issues.definition: When a vesting dispute concerns a landholder that holds the land as a non-agricultural tenant, that landholder is excluded from the intermediary category.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s conditional right to seek transfer of land held by a tenant is not an unreasonable restriction on the right to hold property when it forms part of a scheme balancing landlord and tenant rights.
material_facts: The challenged provision allowed a landlord to seek transfer only when a tenant transferred its rights in the land to a third party.
The right depended on contiguity with land in the landlord’s actual possession and the land being required for a permitted purpose.
The statutory scheme protected tenants’ tenure and made their interests heritable and transferable.
The challenge asserted that the provision imposed an unreasonable restriction on the constitutional right to hold property.
issues.conclusion: The provision did not impose an unreasonable restriction and was constitutionally valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(f) protects the right to hold property, subject to reasonable restrictions. The Court distinguished Bhau Ram v. Baijnath Singh, where the restriction rested solely on vicinage, and relied on Ram Sarup v. Munshi. It held that contiguity was not the sole basis of the challenged right: the statutory scheme secured tenant rights while allowing an immediate landlord, subject to additional conditions, to seek transfer when the tenant transferred the land to a third party. The object was an adjustment of landlord and tenant rights.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_landlord_transfer_right and tenant_interests_are_secure_and_transferable and landlord_right_arises_on_transfer_to_third_party and contiguity_is_required and permitted_landlord_need_is_required

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_landlord_tra: A party challenged the constitutionality of a landlord’s conditional right to seek transfer of land.
predicates.tenant_interests_are_secure_and_transfer: The governing scheme protected tenants against eviction in specified circumstances and allowed their interests to be inherited and transferred.
predicates.landlord_right_arises_on_transfer_to_thi: The landlord’s right arose when a tenant transferred its land rights to a third party.
predicates.contiguity_is_required: The landlord could exercise the right only if the transferred land adjoined land in the landlord’s actual possession.
predicates.permitted_landlord_need_is_required: The landlord could exercise the right only if the land was required for a permitted purpose.

issues.definition: When a challenged landlord transfer right operates within a scheme securing transferable tenant interests and is conditioned on a third-party transfer, contiguity, and a permitted need, the restriction is reasonable.
